web.description:
# Work out if you have to pay super
## When super guarantee is required
- Employee age – for employees who are
  - [under 18 years old](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/super-for-employers/work-out-if-you-have-to-pay-super#Employeesagedunder18), you pay super if they work more than 30 hours in a week.

## Employees under 18
Employees under 18 years old are eligible for super guarantee if they work for you for more than 30 hours in a week, regardless of how much you pay them.

### Example: under 18 years old and working different hours a week
- more than 30 hours in one week in the hardware store, this employer pays her super guarantee for this week

## Domestic or private workers
Domestic or private workers are eligible for super guarantee if they work for you for more than 30 hours in a week, regardless of how much you pay them.

# Super from your employer
## Super guarantee eligibility
- full time, part time or casual – except if you're
  - [under 18 years old](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/super-for-employers/work-out-if-you-have-to-pay-super#ato-Employeesunder18), you're only eligible for super guarantee if you work more than 30 hours in a week
  - paid to do work of a private or domestic nature, you're only eligible for super guarantee if you work more than 30 hours in a week

web.title: What payments are qualifying earnings | Australian Taxation Office
web.description:
# What payments are qualifying earnings
## Payments that are not qualifying earnings
- [payments to employees under 18 and domestic or private workers](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/super-for-employers/paying-super-on-payday/what-payments-are-qualifying-earnings#Employeesunder18anddomesticorpriva) unless they work more than 30 hours in a week

### Employees under 18 and domestic or private workers
You do not need to pay super guarantee on payments to an employee who is under 18 years old, or a private or domestic worker, in any week where the employee or worker doesn't work more than 30 hours.

web.title: Superannuation for Under 18s - Rest Super
web.description:
# Superannuation for under 18s ## Do I get paid super if I’m under 18? Here's the deal: if you're a minor and you work more than 30 hours a week, your employer generally has to pay you SG contributions, no matter how much you earn – even if you’re paid in cash. Each week, she works 31 hours.
- At the supermarket, he works 32 hours a week. | | | |-|-| | Case study: Nia works 31 hours a week | Nia is 16 years old and is completing an electrician apprenticeship program. Each week, she works 31 hours. This means she is eligible for SG payments from her employer. | | Case study: Kamal works different hours each week | Kamal is 17 years old and works two jobs: at the supermarket and at his uncle’s café. 
- At the supermarket, he works 32 hours a week. This means he is eligible for SG payments from this employer.
- When he has time, he also covers shifts at his uncle’s café on a [casual basis](https://rest.com.au/super/learn/employment/casual-and-part-time-employees), adding 4-6 hours a fortnight. This means his uncle doesn’t need to pay him SG. |

web.title: Override under-18 superannuation qualifying earnings in a pay run
web.description:
However, currently, employees under 18 are only entitled to superannuation if they work more than 30 hours per week in a given week.

### [Override qualifying earnings in a pay run](https://help.employmenthero.com/hc/en-au/articles/17426659155215-Override-under-18-superannuation-qualifying-earnings-in-a-pay-run#h_step_by_step)
2. Enter the correct Qualifying Earnings amount:
   - Enter **0** if the employee did not work more than 30 hours in any single week during the pay period and is therefore not entitled to super for this period. ![Screenshot showing 0 entered into the override field](https://employmenthero.zendesk.com/hc/article_attachments/16621123982351)
   - Enter the actual qualifying earnings amount if the employee worked more than 30 hours in at least one week and super is owed on that portion. ![Screenshot showing an adjusted amount entered into the override field](https://employmenthero.zendesk.com/hc/article_attachments/16621139209231)
